prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 华东区门店2024年1—5月销量 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "门店" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 92px
  col 2: header "1月" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 3: header "2月" · longest unbreakable word 34px · one-line width 34px
  col 4: header "3月" · longest unbreakable word 34px · one-line width 34px
  col 5: header "4月" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 6: header "5月" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare monthly sales across East China stores and reveal each store's month-to-month trend over January–May.","reading":"Readers scan row by row to identify a store, then read left to right across the five months; they also compare a single month vertically across stores. The row-label column anchors each row, while the month columns form one continuous comparable series.","groups":["Column 1 (门店): row-label column identifying each store.","Columns 2–6 (1月–5月): one comparable time series; keep near-equal widths and consistent alignment so month-to-month differences read cleanly."],"keep_intact":["Month headers 1月–5月, unbroken.","All numeric sales values, with no wrapping, truncation, or overflow.","门店 header and the full characters of every store name; store names may wrap but must not be truncated."],"may_wrap":["Store names such as 上海徐汇店 and 南京新街口店 may wrap at Chinese character boundaries; row height can absorb two lines.","Month headers and numbers should not wrap."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[81,56,55,55,56,56],"idea":"Prioritize row labels: keep every month column at its one-line minimum and give 门店 the remaining 81px, so store names wrap at four characters."},{"name":"B","widths":[74,57,57,57,57,57],"idea":"Balance both roles with a regular 57px month grid and a 74px row-label column, accepting slightly more wrapping in store names."},{"name":"C","widths":[68,58,58,58,58,58],"idea":"Treat the five months as the dominant comparison grid: equal 58px columns give numbers more air, while 门店 shrinks to 68px and store names wrap at three characters."}]}
